parsed.explanation: The state layer is strongly protective: gender identity/expression covered in public accommodations, housing, employment since 2012–2016 (ballot-retained), a hate-crime statute with a reporting unit, self-ID documents, a care shield law, and a July 2026 'Most Protective' ranking. But the combined regime includes the federal layer: binary sex definition, visa refusal on any document discrepancy, possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, foreign travel advisories against the country, federal building facility bans, and documented abuse in federal immigration custody (beatings, sexual abuse) plus conversion-therapy-style federal prison policy. Unenforceable sodomy wording and absent repeal are tangential. State protections bound most daily exposure; federal entry and custody exposures cap the score below the 0.85 tier.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal February 2025 cable instructs officers to refuse cases where documents cast doubt on sex, demand extra evidence, and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; X markers barred; trans travellers report blocked/confiscated passports and being stranded; eight foreign governments issued advisories. Documented.
entry_documents.protection: State issues its own self-ID documents (X licence/ID since 2019, X birth certificates 2024, confidential name changes 2025), but these do not govern federal entry screening.
entry_documents.interaction: State self-ID cannot cure a federal visa/entry refusal; a visitor passes state lines but is screened once by federal officers at the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody documents forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees; federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policy (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026 and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State hate-crime statute (gender identity since 2012) with a reporting unit, police and justice-department involvement; no state criminalisation of trans presence or facilities use; 2025 restroom arrest occurred elsewhere.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained federally (entry dispute, offence) enters the hostile federal custody regime, where state protections do not reach; state remedies apply only to state-level encounters.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; national map shows widening state bans (21 units with some ban, 4 states with criminal penalties), including one documented 2025 trespass arrest with 24 hours held in the men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state has no facility ban; public-accommodation law (effective 2016, retained 67.8% in 2018) covers hotels, restaurants, shops, transport — the settings a visitor actually uses.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State law governs private venues; federal building bans (post offices, courthouses, federal sites) still apply inside the state and have no state override.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders and October 2025 proposed rules target gender-affirming care, especially for minors; DOJ subpoenaed 'over 20' hospitals for under-19 patient records in summer 2025; federal insurance restrictions pending.
care_services.protection: State shield law (2022) protects patients and providers from out-of-state civil/criminal claims; 2022 codified gender-affirming care protections; conversion therapy on minors banned; relevant for a visiting family.
care_services.interaction: State shield covers state providers, but does not block federal subpoenas or federal funding conditions reaching the same records.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal rhetoric and machinery: 'chemical and surgical mutilation' framing, orders to investigate schools and prosecute teachers facilitating social transition, counterterrorism strategy targeting 'radically pro-transgender' groups, cash-reward memo using 'radical gender ideology' language; 66% public support for birth-sex document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State officials, hate-crime task force and equality bodies operate under protective statutes; state legislature repeatedly advanced repeal of sodomy provisions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises the probability of scrutiny at entry and in federal facilities even where street and state-level treatment is accepting.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal orders criminalising facilitation of a trans minor's social transition, DOJ hospital-record subpoenas for under-19s, and proposed federal insurance bans create risk for a travelling family seeking care or schooling; 27 states ban youth gender-affirming care.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield law, 2019 conversion-therapy ban, protected public accommodations, and the state's 'Most Protective' tier status protect a visiting minor within state borders.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family's state-protected care visit can still be exposed to federal record demands or, if entering federally funded settings, federal facility and funding rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of anti-trans violence or police hostility in this state in the dossier; national bias statistics cover sexual orientation generally.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity hate crimes punishable since 2012 with mandated collection and public reporting via police, justice department and legislative committees, plus a standing task force; public accommodations enforcement machinery exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State recourse is real and operative, unlike in states lacking coverage; background general crime remains outside scope.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal passport litigation, executive-order challenges and October 2025 rules unresolved; several orders blocked/enjoined, so exposure varies by travel date. Unrepealed sodomy/anality provisions remain nominally applicable to a relationship read as same-sex, though unenforceable since 1974.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working state courts, ballot-verified protections, legal-aid FAQ on passport rules, functioning hate-crime reporting and a retained equality framework.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State remedies cannot reverse a federal entry refusal or custody treatment; federal outcomes are contingent and temporally uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Nothing here approaches Varnalia: no routine arrest for document mismatch, no months in pretrial custody, no coerced confessions or capital provision. The worst federal outcomes are entry refusal, a possible fraud finding, and contingent custody abuse — serious but not the sustained imprisonment-and-violence pathway of 0.15.

Luskaine's frontline officers applying outdated checklists despite protective federal rules resembles this dossier's federal entry friction with working advocacy help. This jurisdiction's in-country state layer is stronger (ballot-retained public accommodations, shield law), but its federal custody and facility exposures are more severe than a mere form delay.

Meridia's trained border staff, brief detention, working tribunal and compensation mirrors this state's functioning remedies — but entry here carries a documented refusal-on-discrepancy cable and possible lifetime ineligibility, plus foreign advisories against the country. Comparable overall because the state's daily-life protections are broader than Meridia's.

Aldermere's guarantee of care with enforceable ombuds and licence sanctions exceeds this state federally: here federal orders, record subpoenas and facility bans remain operative and reachable inside the state. The state layer alone would sit near 0.85; the federal layer is what pulls the combined regime down.

parsed.synthesis: Two regimes interact. Inside state borders the visitor meets genuinely operative protections: public-accommodation coverage retained by a 67.8% vote, hate-crime reporting machinery, self-ID state documents, a care shield law, and a 'Most Protective' ranking — these bound hotel, restaurant, shop, transport and state-clinic exposure, so routine daily life is low-risk. Above that sits a hostile federal layer no state law pre-empts: binary-sex documents, visa refusal on any discrepancy, possible lifetime fraud findings, federal-building facility bans, and documented abuse in federal immigration custody. Contingency matters — most visitors with clean passports clear entry and never enter federal custody — but the entry and custody exposures are documented, state-implemented, and without a state-level remedy. Net: reduced risk with a real federal tail, above 0.65-tier friction jurisdictions, below the 0.85 protective tier.
